blind_spots.blind_spot: Perceptive, the wearable that shares its physiological-sensing core with the Army SBIR effort, is described as needing constant cloud connectivity with no field-connectivity fallback discussed.
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Automatically connects to the cloud to deliver important health metrics' assumes constant uplink — the same failure mode as the 30fps crowd-detection case if this is meant to report a warfighter's vitals from a DDIL environment with no reliable connection.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Core product and marketing are built for consumer eldercare, not defense deployment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Perceptive automatically connects to the cloud to deliver important health metrics without the need for an app or cell phone.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Proximity, the buried perimeter sensor, is marketed as standalone early-warning security with no mention of how an alert reaches a command post or common operating picture.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A buried sensor that detects but never states how it feeds a unit's TAK/C2 picture stays a local gadget — 'operators loving it is not adoption.'
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product is pitched at commercial/civilian perimeter-security buyers, not built into a military C2 integration story.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Buried underground, it acts as an early-warning perimeter security system.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No visible hiring toward compliance, ITAR, or field-test roles despite holding a military-applications SBIR, and no jobs data in the pack at all.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Without a credible team building toward Phase II transition support (test, compliance, field integration), a small Phase I award risks lapsing before the product ever reaches an operator.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Small, long-running company (founded 2011, 11-50 employees) likely running lean on core hardware/firmware rather than adding new compliance headcount.

opener_hook: Matrix Industries holds an Army SBIR for self-powered wearable physiological sensors — how does Perceptive's cloud-dependent design hold up in a DDIL field environment?
what_they_do: Self-powered (body-heat/solar/thermal energy-harvesting) sensors — a health wearable (Perceptive) and a buried perimeter-detection sensor (Proximity) — sold commercially, with an Army SBIR exploring military physiological-monitoring use.
